hook.text: How you remove the fruit from the seed changes the coffee's flavor as much as where it was grown.

buildup.text: Washed (wet): pulp is removed, beans ferment in water tanks, then dry. Result: clean, bright flavors.

discovery.text: Natural (dry): whole cherries dry in the sun for weeks. Fruit sugars soak into the bean—fruity, winey flavors.

twist.text: Honey process: pulp is removed but mucilage stays on during drying. It bridges clean and fruity profiles.

climax.text: Experimental processes—anaerobic fermentation, carbonic maceration—push flavor boundaries even further.

punchline.text: Same bean, different process, completely different cup.

quiz.question: What defines 'natural' coffee processing?
options: Whole cherries dry in the sun with fruit intact

details.summary: After picking, coffee cherries are processed to extract the bean. The three main methods are washed, which removes all fruit before drying; natural, which dries the whole cherry; and honey, which leaves some mucilage on the bean. Each method creates distinctly different flavors.
details.whyItMatters: Processing has as much impact on flavor as origin or variety. It is one of the most important variables in specialty coffee quality.
takeaways: Washed processing produces clean, bright flavor profiles
Natural processing creates fruity, fuller-bodied coffees
Honey processing balances sweetness and clarity

faq.question: Which processing method produces the best coffee?
faq.answer: There is no single best method. Washed coffees highlight origin character with clarity. Natural coffees offer intense fruit flavors. Honey coffees blend sweetness with body. Personal preference and the specific coffee variety determine which tastes best to each drinker.

faq.question: Why do most specialty coffees use washed processing?
faq.answer: Washed processing removes variables from the fruit layer, producing consistent and transparent flavors that showcase terroir. It requires clean water and infrastructure, making it more expensive but more predictable for quality-focused producers.
